title: No monthly subscription options
body: You might want to consider a monthly subscription option. Theres no way I’m paying $150NZD yearly. In this economy??
author: Leasha in nz

title: The only to do list my child can follow
body:
I got the Joon app for my child, and she has been consistently completing her tasks. She is motivated to finish them in order to earn rewards, and she loves playing with her virtual pet! 

However, I still need to remind her to do her chores, and I’m concerned that the app may be increasing her screen time, which is a downside for me. 

Other than that, Joon is a great app that helps my neurodivergent child get things done in a fun way. 😊

title: Happy ADHD parent
body: This has been a great app for getting my son to have some motivation to do chores and get to school classes. The school has also seen some quick improvement with engagement by my son in school.

title: Amazing
body: I wish I had found this earlier. No more fights, or trying to manage my child’s deregulation. She runs to complete her quests and asks for new ones. I totally recommend this app for anyone that has tried multiple ways to help their child.
author: Chchgal62805

title: Customer support and responsivity
body: I found it was easy to contact customer support with my initial thoughts about how the app was working for my family. They were very helpful and responsive. We’re also finding that the joon game app is highly motivating for our children, and it’s easy to create new quests and rewards. The app has been shifting the needle for us in making parenting more positive again!
author: Eschoom

title: You need this app
body: This app is great! I love it and my kids want to check their pets several times a day. It’s been helping them a lot with chores they normally would turn their noses up at. They look forward to each egg. Install it! You won’t regret it!
author: CeeCee253

title: Joon for my 3 older kids, AsD and ADHD in the family
body:
Started to do joon a few weeks back. Since then I have seen a night and day improvement with my kids executive functioning. It used to be all I could do to get them to tidy their rooms after school or do their daily job, and forget making beds or even brushing teeth. Nag nag nag. Now however, my kids are motivating themselves to get stuff done to get coins. One has like 8 pets so far, another 5. The more they do the game, I need to put a few extra things on for them to earn more. 

But it doesn’t have to be jobs to put on, either. It can be mental health stuff, or exercise, etc, to get a few more coins in a fun way. I have one for the kids to finish their school drink bottle, bc they were getting migraines. 

They can play games, it’s sort of like neopets from the early 2000’s. You can set rewards for them to purchase with their coins as well. And if you really want to, I’m sure you could put yourself as a child too! 

We have AsD, adhd, Irlens x2, probable dyslexia, dyspraxia, and other stuff in our family to contend with. Believe me this isn’t a neurotypical family! And it works!
author: Johnophia

title: It’s working well
body: ADHD household, and this is working well so far for our 2 boys. It does require a bit of time to set it up just how you want it, but then it’s smooth sailing.
author: Nicknamedforyou

title: I love this app.
body: My son has ADHD and it’s so hard to get him to complete tasks, I’m always nagging and reminding. This helps with the mental load. I loaded in the whole morning routine, and now he’s doing it himself. I added in lots of extras and custom quests for particular days and it’s amazing. This morning he got up, opened all the curtains and blinds, made himself toast, packed his school bag… He’s 6! I want a doter for me too…

title: Don’t Do It
body: All the ads promise the world, and app ends up being so basic. I thought would be perfect for my ND gamer kids but they are so bored it’s no motivation at all! For the money it cost me $80+nzd I was expecting a better faster app and just more to it. So disappointed.
author: Rephastie

title: Joon review
body: Pretty good! A bit fiddly for the kid, but a good tool in the ‘motivation toolbox’ for adhd. You have to try it out really. Every kid is different.
author: Andrw.ds

title: Surprisingly engaging
body: I’m using Joon for a 10 year old and a 12 year old. The 10 year old has classic ADHD and the 12 year old has inattentive ADHD and low support ASD. I was a bit apprehensive about another new app that claims a lot and at first the 12 year old stated she wasn’t going to use it!! But once I’d set custom rewards that include fun family activities that she did want she has become really engaged in checking for quests, doing them and claiming rewards. The younger one is enjoying the game aspect of the app and I can’t believe that she’s actually saying things like “oh, I’ve gotto unload the dishwasher now because I want the coins”!! I’ve got ADHD too and the app is helping my planning and management and making day to day life easier because I don’t have to argue or even ask anymore. I guess it take the onus off and onto them. I’ve never been able to maintain star charts or my routines beyond the ones necessary to meet external obligations, like school. So so far Joon is flipping awesome. Thanks heaps to the devs. Single mum from AOTEAROA (New Zealand)
author: vividConfusion

title: Amazing
body: This app has been a godsend with having 2 adhd mornings are hard !!! But since using the app things have got way easier !!! My kids love being able to interact with their pet so to do that they need to do their chores . Yay for Joon !!! Thank you !!!

body: I’ve found this app helpful with getting my kids involved in household tasks. What’s great is that it has age appropriate suggestions already loaded, and not all are chores, e.g. “ask a parent how their day was” which is a really good habit to practice.
